question: What does the insert helper at 0x5f90bb0, left open as 'rehash internals' by RE-001-distinct-key-sum-115, do end to end: its two find phases, its insert linking, its rehash trigger, its result pair and its exception cleanup?
semantics: insert(table, holder): key = [holder]; if [table + 0x18] (element count) is non-zero, find by bucket chain: b = key % [table + 0x8] (unsigned), pred = buckets[b]; if pred is set, walk the chain from pred's next node while each following node still hashes to b, returning (node, false) on a key match at [node + 0x8]; if the count is zero, find by a linear scan of the whole list from [table + 0x10], returning (node, false) on a match, with b computed only afterwards. On a miss: allocate a 16-byte node (next = 0, [node + 0x8] = [holder]), save [table + 0x28], ask _M_need_rehash(policy = table + 0x20, bucket count, element count, 1); if it answers grow, call the rehash body 0x5da04d0 (table, new count, &saved) and recompute b; then link: if buckets[b] is set, insert the node after that predecessor (predecessor's next becomes the node, node's next becomes the old successor); else make the node the new list head, set buckets[old head's bucket] to the node when a head existed, and set buckets[b] to the before-begin slot (table + 0x10). Increment the element count and return (node, true). The stack canary is checked before every return. On exception from the need_rehash/rehash call range (LSDA row 0x5f90cb1..0x5f90d1b) the landing pad at 0x5f90d66 jumps to the shared cleanup block 0x5f90b86, which deletes the new node and resumes unwinding; a throw from the node allocation itself has no pad.
